intro: **Your DGX Spark. Your team's AI workspace.** Team AI Box turns one NVIDIA DGX Spark into a browser-based workspace for local AI, shared files, communication and virtual devices. It is built for teams that want to own their deployment and use the same tools from multiple computers, without installing a separate AI stack on every desk.
why: **One appliance, one workspace.** AI tools, collaboration and virtual devices share a consistent interface and account system.
**Local-first AI.** Run model inference on your Spark and optionally connect external model APIs.
**Built for DGX Spark.** Install on Ubuntu ARM64 with NVIDIA GPU containers and KVM virtualization.
**Yours to improve.** Original code is MIT licensed. The interface supports 17 languages, light/dark themes and persistent manual language choices; English is the default.
installTitle: Install on a fresh DGX Spark
requirements: Use a **fresh DGX Spark with Ubuntu 24.04 ARM64**, working Docker Engine + Compose v2, NVIDIA drivers/container support, KVM, Git and Python 3.10+. Allow several hundred GB of temporary free space for models, container builds and the package. Do not run a fresh installation over existing business data.
installExplanation: Run these commands **on the Spark**, not on a desktop laptop. The installer downloads model/build inputs, builds runtime images, creates a complete offline package and installs it. This first source build requires internet access and substantial download/build time; clone alone does not install the product. Docker and the NVIDIA environment are reused, not replaced.
resume: `--check` performs preflight. If interrupted, keep `/var/tmp/teamaibox-source-build` and rerun the **same command**: verified downloads and completed stages are reused. Do not start competing builds or delete the cache. Official sources are the default. Where upstream access is unavailable, use the documented alternate-source options or transfer a verified cache/complete offline package from a connected machine; no mirror guarantees availability. See [source installation](install/SOURCE-INSTALL.md) for logs, `--cache-dir`, `--work-dir` and recovery. A changed source tree needs a separate work directory, not a bypassed checkpoint.
first: Open `https://<BOX_LAN_IP>/` using the Spark's current LAN address. Verify that its locally generated HTTPS certificate belongs to your device.
Sign in as `admin` / `admin`, **change the initial password**, then create ordinary accounts. Do not expose the initial credentials to the public internet.
Wait for each AI application to become ready, select a language/theme in the profile menu and begin from the workbench.

For virtual computers, provide your own authorized Windows/Linux ARM64 ISO and OS license. For an offline target, first prepare the complete package, then follow [the package installation guide](install/README.md); source preparation itself is not offline.
limits: Original code and documentation are MIT licensed, **not every binary in an installation**. Third-party code, model weights, NVIDIA components, firmware, Google services and Windows retain their own terms. The repository does not ship model weights, installed Android/Windows disks, signed-in accounts, ISOs or offline packages. Google compatibility is not Play Protect certification; casting does not cover DRM-protected content or Apple certification. Windows 10 ARM64 is not claimed as supported. Performance and concurrency depend on workloads and hardware.
contribute: We welcome bug reports, documentation, translations, accessibility improvements, application integrations and code. Start with an issue describing the user problem, fork the repository, create a focused branch and submit a pull request with relevant checks and screenshots. You do not need to own a Spark to improve docs or isolated components; label hardware-dependent results honestly. Never attach secrets, personal files or signed-in device images. Report vulnerabilities privately through SECURITY.md, not a public issue. No mandatory CLA or paid contributor permission is required.
